text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of 429s for a subset of orgs. Digging shows enforcer counters are ahead of the metering sink (writes lag ~90-120s).
Maria Gomez: ugh. are those per-key or per-org buckets?
Alex Chen: per-org buckets primarily, but some API keys also hit burst controls. The enforcer reads from Redis counts updated by the realtime writer, but writer -> kafka -> sink has a processing delay and occasionally backpressure.
Jordan Patel: any chance enforcer is using cached/derived counts that don't expire quickly?
Alex Chen: yep, enforcer kept local in-memory aggregate + Redis keys with 5m TTL. That means if the sink is slow, the enforcer denies requests before the ledger catches up.
Jihoon Kim: can we switch enforcer to a conservative mode: prefer allowance when sink lag detected? i.e., bias towards letting requests through if the last sink watermark < now - 60s.
Maria Gomez: that could work. We should be careful about abuse though — need a fallback to avoid unbounded overage. maybe allow a small additive burst allowance per-org while we reconcile.
Sarah Lee: quick mitigation: roll the enforcer config to use `burst_window_seconds = 10` and `counter_ttl = 30s` so counters are fresher. Also enable a short grace token of +200 tokens for monitored orgs.
Jordan Patel: how do we detect "lag" reliably? we can add a metric: `metering.sink_lag_seconds` from the consumer. If > 30s for an org, flip that org into temporary lenient mode.
Alex Chen: agree. adding metric first is low-risk. We can QA by replaying requests into a staging sink and toggling.
enforcer-bot: deploy plan queued: change default `counter_ttl=30s` in canary -> staging -> prod.
Maria Gomez: log sample for context:
```
[2026-06-12T14:03:21Z] enforcer: org=acme-corp key=sk-xxx allow=false reason=burst_exceeded counter=490 window=60s
[2026-06-12T14:04:05Z] meter-sink: org=acme-corp committed=330 total_window=60s lag=85s
```
Alex Chen: see how enforcer saw 490 but sink committed 330 and lagged 85s. that's exactly the divergence.
Jihoon Kim: long-term fix: change source-of-truth for enforcement to read the pre-aggregated kafka topic that the sink writes (materialized view), rather than local in-memory + redis. then both enforcement and billing use the same commit stream.
Sarah Lee: timeline? moving enforcer to consume the same topic is ~2w dev + schema validation. We can do a short stopgap in 2h (config canary) and a medium-term change (1 week) to reduce TTL+add lag metric.
Jordan Patel: also add an enforcement reconciliation job that scans write-ahead logs and repairs counters for orgs that were denied in the last 5m. run as a cron every 5m.
Maria Gomez: for safety we should: 1) canary TTL change to 30s for <10% traffic, 2) enable `metering.sink_lag_seconds` alert at 30s, 3) create a temporary grace bucket for affected orgs, 4) implement reconciliation job.
Alex Chen: I'll own the canary + metrics (will open PR now). Jihoon can own the topic-consumer refactor, Jordan will do the reconciliation job. Sarah will coordinate rollout windows with infra.
Jihoon Kim: noted. I'll sketch consumer schema compatibility and a small shim to ensure idempotency.
enforcer-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/enforcer/pull/312 — config TTL change + lag metric.
Maria Gomez: thanks. once PR is green, let's schedule canary at 15:30 UTC. please post quick postmortem if we see any customer impact. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: will do. thanks all.
